newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends easy against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends easy against dollar.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed a shade soft against the dollar on Wednesday, after moving in a tight range as high call rates supported the local currency by keeping the dollar down, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.27 after opening at 58.25, they said.

"Movements of the rupee were range-bound because at 58.25 it was already at the Central Bank's buying price. The other end was capped by a lack of demand for dollars," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The Central Bank's dollar-rupee exchange rate was at 58.2541 and 59.4309.
Overnight call money rates closed at 18.5 after opening at 17 and reaching 19, dealers said.

Money is tight due to the cumulative effect of quarterly tax payments, a number of holidays, import covering with dollars from the Central Bank and fortnightly treasury bond auctions of 500 million rupees a time, dealers said.
